title: Trains to Ayr
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the International Ayr Show. ScotRail runs a train from Glasgow Central to Ayr every half an hour, through Paisley, and the coast lines bring you in from Largs, Girvan and Stranraer too. I’ve added the connections that work well, like the trains from Edinburgh, and Avanti West Coast and TransPennine Express from London Euston, Carlisle and Preston, with a change at Glasgow Central. If you’re starting on the c2c line, from Shoeburyness, Southend, Basildon, Grays or anywhere along to Barking, I’ve added those stations too, with the change in London. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the Ayr Show. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From the station it’s about 15 to 20 minutes on foot. Walk down Fort Street and through Wellington Square to the Esplanade, and the Low Green is right in front of you. On show days the streets are busy, so you can just follow the crowd.
walkBack: Allow about 20 minutes to walk back up to the station from the Low Green, and a bit more when the crowds leave, especially after the Friday evening show.
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows trains run by ScotRail, plus the Avanti West Coast and TransPennine Express trains that connect with them. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Friday 6 and Saturday 7 November 2026, checked on 1 November 2026. The big stations and city termini further from Ayr use the times for Friday 13 and Saturday 14 November 2026, checked on 10 November 2026. These are this winter’s times, and the summer 2027 times will follow, so please check with ScotRail before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. text: If you’re coming from London, Edinburgh, Carlisle or Preston, you’ll most likely change at Glasgow Central. When I last checked, the change there was usually about {typ} minutes, and between {min} and {max} minutes on the trains on this page.
It’s a big station. I would head for the departure boards as soon as you get off and keep an eye on them, as platforms can change on the day.

In 2026 there was a queue system at Glasgow Central before the show, so on the Saturday morning I would allow longer than the timetable says. On the way home you change here again, and the trains back from Ayr fill up once the flying finishes, so give yourself plenty of time for that connection.

x.busyTip: Ayr station is at its busiest straight after the flying display ends, and in 2026 there was a queue system for the trains back. I would suggest waiting a while and getting some food in town while the queues go down. If you aren’t waiting for the last display, you could leave before it starts. Check your last train time just below before you settle in, especially on the Friday evening.

about.Glasgow Central|Paisley Gilmour Street: Out of Central over the Clyde and west through the edge of the city to Paisley.
about.Paisley Gilmour Street|Kilwinning: Out into the Renfrewshire countryside, past Castle Semple Loch at Lochwinnoch, then down through Glengarnock and Dalry into Ayrshire.
about.Kilwinning|Ayr: Down the Ayrshire coast through Irvine and Troon, with Arran across the water on a clear day. You pass Prestwick Airport just before Ayr, so keep an eye out for aircraft.
about.Largs|Kilwinning: Along the Firth of Clyde through Fairlie and West Kilbride, with Great Cumbrae and Arran out to the side.
about.Kilmarnock|Ayr: Across Ayrshire to Barassie, then down the coast through Troon and past Prestwick Airport, so keep an eye out for aircraft.
about.Kilmarnock|Glasgow Central: Through Stewarton and Barrhead into the south side of Glasgow.
about.Girvan|Ayr: Up the Carrick coast through Maybole.
about.Stranraer|Girvan: Over the hills of Galloway through Barrhill. It’s one of the quietest lines in Scotland, with long stretches of moorland.
about.Carlisle|Kilmarnock: Up Nithsdale through Dumfries and Sanquhar, then over the hills to Kilmarnock.
about.Carlisle|Glasgow Central: Up the West Coast Main Line over Beattock Summit, through Lockerbie and Motherwell.
about.Carlisle|Motherwell: Up the West Coast Main Line over Beattock Summit, through Lockerbie.
about.Motherwell|Glasgow Central: The last few miles into Glasgow along the Clyde valley.
about.Preston|Carlisle: Up the West Coast Main Line past Lancaster and over Shap, with the Lake District fells off to the west.
about.Edinburgh Waverley|Glasgow Central: Across the middle of Scotland, through Shotts or Carstairs depending on the train.
about.Edinburgh Waverley|Motherwell: Across the middle of Scotland on the Shotts line.
about.London Euston|Preston: The West Coast Main Line between London and Preston, through the Midlands and Cheshire.

pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, especially from England, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. They can sell out, so I would book as soon as the summer times are out.
The same fare all day on ScotRail

When I last checked, ScotRail fares cost the same whatever time you travel, so on the ScotRail part of your trip you can catch whichever train suits you. Coming from England, the time rules on Avanti West Coast and TransPennine Express tickets still apply, so check those before you buy.

A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, and it can pay for itself in one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Which station is closest to the show?

Ayr. It’s about a 15 to 20 minute walk down Fort Street and through Wellington Square to the Low Green. Newton-on-Ayr is the stop before, but it’s further from the Low Green, so I would stay on to Ayr.
Do I need a ticket for the show?
No. The International Ayr Show is free to watch, so it’s only the train fare to think about. The adults only Friday Flightline and Saturday Chill Out Zone are booked separately if you want a seat.
Friday 3 and Saturday 4 September 2027. The Friday is an evening display and the Saturday a full afternoon, so I would pick your train for the day you’re going.
Will there be extra trains on show days?
In 2026 ScotRail ran three trains an hour from Glasgow Central on the Saturday, with an hourly express and extra carriages. The 2027 plans aren’t out yet, so please check nearer the time.
I’m coming from Edinburgh. Is there a quicker way?

The times on this page change at Glasgow Central. Some people take the faster train to Glasgow Queen Street and walk across the city centre to Central, which takes about 10 minutes. I have left that off this page, as it isn’t a train all the way.
Can I get there and back from London in a day?

It’s about 6 hours each way, with a change at Glasgow Central, so it makes for a very long day. When I last checked, the last train that gets you back to London Euston the same night left Ayr at 17:05 on the Friday and 16:21 on the Saturday, and both of those go before the flying finishes. I would think about staying the night in Ayr or Glasgow, and book early, as show weekend is busy.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
